diagnostic_evidence.quote: Property (i) is a direct consequence of optimization.
Update $\theta$ of $\bu^{n+1}_\theta$ by minimizing the JKO loss $\ell^{n+1}$ \eqref{jko_loss} using Algorithm \ref{algorithm_opt}.

issues.failure_explanation: Entropy dissipation (Props. prop:added-3/prop:added-4(i)) is derived by comparing the exact minimizer of the particle loss with u=0 (loss 0), i.e. it requires ell^{n+1}(theta) <= 0. Algorithm 1 outputs a network after finitely many SGD epochs (Theorem thm_opt_conv only bounds gradient norms of a nonconvex loss in theta), so ell^{n+1}(theta_K) <= 0 is not guaranteed; moreover the random-batch update in Sec. 4.3 replaces the full sums h_i by in-batch sums, breaking the identity sum_i h_i = -(tau/N) sum_{ij} h_{ij} used in the proof. 'Unconditional stability' is asserted but proved nowhere.

failure_location.quote: the proposed method enjoys exact entropy dissipation and unconditional stability

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the claims to the exact minimizer/full update, or add an acceptance check ell^{n+1}(theta_K) <= 0 (falling back to u=0 otherwise) so that the discrete entropy inequality holds for the implemented method, and remove or prove the stability claim.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract/intro/conclusion guarantees of exact entropy decay and unconditional stability apply only to exact minimizers with full-particle updates, not to the algorithm as implemented (finite SGD training, warm start, random-batch updates).
issues.title: "Exact entropy dissipation" and "unconditional stability" claimed for the implemented method, but only proved for exact minimizers with full-batch updates
issues.why_classification: A short qualification or a one-line acceptance test restores a verifiable entropy inequality for the implemented scheme; the propositions themselves remain correct.

issues.failure_explanation: Applying the adjoint identity (new_div) to the weak form (0910) gives d/dt ∫φf = +½∫φ ∇̃·(ff_*∇̃ δH/δf), i.e. ∂_t f − ½∇̃·(ff_*∇̃ δH/δf) = 0. Equation (landau_weak3) has the opposite sign, so with the stated definitions it reads ∂_t f = −Q(f,f), contradicting (landau_homo). The same sign propagates to the constraint in (dL); the derivation 'Then (dL-new) directly follows from (dL)' actually yields ∂_t f = −∇·[f∫A(u−u_*)f_*], the opposite of (dL-new).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign in (new_div) (or equivalently in (landau_weak3) and the constraint of (dL)) so the conventions match (landau_homo) and (dL-new).
issues.overall_effect: Definitions in Sections 1–2.1 are mutually inconsistent; the metric d_L is invariant under V→−V so no later result changes, but the stated identification of (dL) with (dL-new) is off by a sign.
issues.title: Sign inconsistency between the divergence convention (new_div), the weak form (0910), and the rewritten Landau equation (landau_weak3)/(dL)
issues.why_classification: Purely a convention fix with a choice of where to flip; all downstream formulations and results are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Of particular interest is the case when $d = 3$ and $\gamma = -3$

issues.failure_explanation: All particle formulas (djko_p), (djko_p2), (update_v), (update_f) and the loss (jko_loss) sum over j=1..N including j=i. For γ<0 the factor |v_i−v_j|^γ is infinite at j=i, and for γ+2<0 (Coulomb, γ=−3) A(0) itself is undefined, so h_{i,i} = A(0):∇u(v_i) − ∞·0 is not defined; the scheme as written is ill-defined for the soft-potential regime the paper targets and tests.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict all double sums to j≠i (consistent with the diagonal having measure zero in the continuum) or state a convention for the diagonal terms; conservation and entropy-dissipation proofs are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The particle formulation, loss, and update rules are not well defined for γ<0; the stated Coulomb experiments must rely on an unstated convention.
issues.title: Particle sums include the diagonal j=i terms, which are undefined for soft potentials (γ<0, in particular Coulomb)
issues.why_classification: A local, routine convention (exclude j=i) repairs well-definedness without altering any result or guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma sgd_lemma2 gives the coefficient αL²B/(2N) in front of Δ, and Lemma sgd_lemma1 gives Δ ≤ α²N²/B²(...). Their product is α³L²N/(2B)(...), but the proof writes α³L²N/(2B²)(...), losing a factor B. Carried through, the noise term should be 6σ²L²α²N/B, not 6σ²L²α²N/B²; the theorem as stated is not what the argument yields (the step-size condition used still suffices for the −1/2 factor).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace N/B² by N/B in the final bound of Theorem thm_opt_conv.
issues.overall_effect: The constant in the stated convergence bound is unsupported by a factor of B (independently of ISSUE-005).
issues.title: Algebra error in the proof of Theorem thm_opt_conv drops a factor B, making the stated bound too small
issues.why_classification: A constant-factor correction with no change in rate or method.

issues.failure_explanation: The last inequality of the proof bounds ‖∇ℓ(θ_k) − ∇ℓ_{ij}(θ^{(k+1)}_{q−1})‖ by L‖θ_k − θ^{(k+1)}_{q−1}‖, but (A.2) only controls ∇ℓ_{ij} against itself; at q=1 the step asserts ∇ℓ_{ij}(θ_k)=∇ℓ(θ_k) for all in-batch pairs, which is false. The reshuffling analysis of \cite{sgd_shffling} relies on a full pass summing to the full gradient, but here an epoch visits only the NB in-batch pairs {(i,j): i,j∈C_q}, not all N² pairs, so (1/(BN))Σ_qΣ_{i,j∈C_q}∇ℓ_{ij}(θ_k) ≠ ∇ℓ(θ_k). The lemma is false as stated: e.g. N=2, B=1, ℓ_{11}=ℓ_{22}=−θ, ℓ_{12}=ℓ_{21}=3θ gives ℓ=θ, ∇ℓ=1, yet the epoch increases ℓ by α while the lemma requires a decrease ≈ α/2. The deterministic per-epoch descent in Theorem thm_opt_conv therefore fails; the estimator is also biased unless the diagonal terms ℓ_{ii} vanish.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the reshuffling-based argument by a stochastic-gradient analysis in expectation that accounts for the in-batch pair sampling (bias of diagonal vs off-diagonal pairs and a variance term), which yields a bound with an O(α σ²)-type noise term and stationarity for the correspondingly reweighted loss.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence guarantee for Algorithm 2 (Theorem thm_opt_conv), including its α² noise floor, is unsupported and the deterministic descent inequality is false in general; only Lemma sgd_lemma1 survives.
issues.title: Lemma sgd_lemma2 (and hence Theorem thm_opt_conv) invalid: in-batch pair gradients do not sum to the full gradient, so the L-smoothness step is unjustified and the reshuffling argument does not apply
issues.why_classification: The entire proof architecture (Lemmas sgd_lemma1–2 as a reshuffling analysis) does not apply to the algorithm; any valid replacement is a different argument and materially worsens the guarantee (noise term α²→α, possible bias), so no comparable version of the stated theorem survives.
